why: Source: read two labelled series for five regions, five divisions, order them and check against options (about 4 steps); question: the same two labelled readings, five sales-to-spend divisions and an ordering (about 4 steps), with no step type added or dropped.
Source: sum 12 labelled revenues, sum 12 headcounts, divide, convert $m to $ (4 steps); question: sum 12 account revenues, sum 12 staff counts, divide, convert $m to $ (4 steps), identical structure.
Source: read two labelled series for five regions, five ratios, ordering (about 4 steps); question: read premiums and running cost for five branches, five ratios, ordering (about 4 steps), same work.

Source: pick the right pie, sum three score shares, multiply by the respondent share of the base (3 steps); question: pick the right pie, sum three shares, multiply by 26% (3 steps), same structure and distractor pies.

Source: read the country's daily customers, daily-to-annual profit, divide cost by annual profit, round up to the first option past break-even (4 steps); question: read daily visitors, annualise profit, divide, round up (4 steps), same trap.

Source: pick the right line, add subcontractor and repair costs, divide by the right wage ignoring the distractor wage, take the largest option within the limit (4 steps); question: identical steps with sofa line and $18 wage (4 steps).
Source: choose the basic rate row, four income-to-dollar divisions, compare (about 3 steps); question: same row choice, four divisions, compare (about 3 steps), with the same PPP distractor row.
Source: read two labelled series for five offices, five ratios, ordering (about 4 steps); question: read fees and promotion budget for five schools, five ratios, ordering (about 4 steps), same work.

Source: read four revenue and four sales-force values off gridlines for the last four years, four divisions, average (about 4 steps); question: the same gridline readings for flexible films, four divisions, average (about 4 steps), with the same distractor series.
Source: sum 12 labelled revenues, sum 12 headcounts, divide, convert $m to $ (4 steps); question: sum 12 studio revenues, sum 12 architect counts, divide, convert (4 steps), identical structure.
